- **Coefficient $C$:** A precomputed scalar satisfying the integral equation to ensure total ray count conservation (magnification balanced by minification) [S2].

The claim states that Coefficient C is a precomputed scalar satisfying an integral equation to ensure total ray count conservation (magnification balanced by minification). The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly defines C via the integral equation ∫[0 to lr] C · sd(s)ds = lr. This equation ensures that the integral of the sampling distance over the lens radius equals the physical radius, which mathematically conserves the total number of rays (or sampling units) mapped across the lens area, thereby balancing the dense sampling (magnification) in the center with the coarse sampling (minification) at the boundary.
